$doc: The securaCV Home Assistant hub image — single source of truth for the native Raspberry Pi hub flasher (docs/design/raspberry_pi_hub_flashing.md). Every fact is derived from an existing source so it can't drift: the base OS version rides the Hub's upstream snapshot, the card floor is parsed from the flasher safety gate (hub_disk.rs), and the baked-in payload is enumerated from the repo's own HA assets. Honest before an image is pinned: the URL is derivable from the version; sha256 stays empty (pinned=false) until the pin ceremony — the same posture as flash.json's all-zero release key.

base_os.name: Home Assistant OS
base_os.why: HAOS is already the self-healing, auto-updating appliance the request asks for: an immutable A/B root (RAUC) that rolls back a bad boot, a Supervisor that watchdogs add-ons, and hands-off OS + add-on updates. We post-process the official image; we do not fork it. See the design doc §4.
base_os.pin_note: sha256 was taken over the actual downloaded asset bytes by the pin ceremony (pin_hub_image.py), cross-checked against GitHub's asset digest where one is published, and is re-verified weekly by --verify in the freshness workflow. A HAOS version bump un-pins until the ceremony re-runs.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit)
boards.usb_device_boot: hold the power button while connecting USB-C (CM5: nRPIBOOT on the IO board)
boards.durable_default: boot from NVMe/SSD (Pi 5) for multi-year endurance

boards.name: Raspberry Pi 4 (64-bit, 4 GB+)
boards.usb_device_boot: connect USB-C with no card inserted (CM4: nRPIBOOT on the IO board; Pi 400: use a card reader)
boards.durable_default: use a high-endurance A2 microSD; watch the SD wear sensor

excluded_boards.why: 1 GB RAM — below the full-stack hub's working set; HAOS runs, this payload doesn't

excluded_boards.model: Raspberry Pi 2 and earlier / Zero family
excluded_boards.why: no 64-bit or too little memory for Home Assistant itself
same image as the 4 GB+ Pi 4, but the payload needs the memory — not a supported hub

card_requirements.note: The exact byte floor is the flasher's safety gate; the human minimum is the supported hardware. A 32 GB card (~29.7 GiB) clears the floor; 16 GB and below are refused.

payload.what: The full-stack pre-bake: the hub boots already wired — no add-on hunting, no restarts.

add_ons.name: Mosquitto broker
add_ons.why: the add-on auto-discovers it (config.yaml services: mqtt:want) and MQTT Discovery needs it

add_ons.name: Frigate NVR
add_ons.why: the recommended camera-detection path (config.yaml mode: frigate). go2rtc — camera restreaming/discovery — is built INTO Frigate; it is not a separate add-on, so it is configured in the Frigate config, not installed.

provisioning.wifi: A NetworkManager keyfile (CONFIG/network/my-network) seeded onto the boot partition — the same secret the Canary flasher already collects (wifi-memory.js). Local-only: it goes on the card, never to a cloud.
provisioning.seed: A curated HA backup, restored at onboarding, brings the payload up pre-wired.
provisioning.self_heal: Inherited from HAOS: A/B rollback + Supervisor watchdog + hands-off updates; our add-on rides the Supervisor update channel.
provisioning.custody: No cloud, nothing phones home; the image is a post-processed pinned official artifact (Inv. IV).
